'''Burgess James Davis''' is an American [[mathematician]] and [[statistician]] known for his research in [[probability theory]] and [[mathematical analysis]], particularly his work on [[martingale (probability theory)|martingales]], [[Brownian motion]], and [[random walk]]s. He is a professor emeritus in the Departments of Statistics and Mathematics at [[Purdue University]].

==Education==
Davis earned his B.S. degree from [[Ohio State University]] in 1965, followed by an M.S. and Ph.D. from the [[University of Illinois]] in 1966 and 1968 respectively.<ref name="PurdueStatCV">{{cite web|title=Burgess Davis - Curriculum Vitae|url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/~bdavis/Davisvita.pdf|publisher=Purdue University Department of Statistics|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref> His doctoral advisor was [[Donald Burkholder]].<ref name="MGP">{{Cite web |title=Burgess James Davis - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=4080 |access-date=November 11, 2025 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

==Career==
He joined the faculty of [[Rutgers University]] from 1968 to 1974. In 1974 he joined [[Purdue University]] where he served as a professor of Statistics and Mathematics until achieving emeritus status in 2014.<ref name="PurdueStatFaculty">{{cite web|title=Emeritus Faculty|url=https://www.stat.purdue.edu/people/faculty/|publisher=Purdue University Department of Statistics|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref>

From 1981 to 1987, Professor Davis served as associate editor of the [[Annals of Probability]], a publication of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], and then as editor from 1991 to 1993.<ref name="AnnalsEditor">{{cite web|title=Past Editors of IMS Publications|url=https://imstat.org/past-editors-of-ims-publications/|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref> He also served as associate editor (from 1988 to 1990) of the [[Transactions of the AMS]] and  (from 1999 to 2002) of the [[Illinois Journal of Math]].<ref name="PurdueStatCV"/>

==Research contributions==
Davis's research focuses on the interconnections between classical analysis (particularly [[harmonic analysis]]), probability theory, and [[stochastic process]]es. His most notable contributions include:
* [[Stochastic analysis]] and [[martingale theory]]: His work established key inequalities for [[stochastic integral]]s and martingales, which includes a strong version of the [[Burkholder–Davis–Gundy inequalities|Burkholder–Gundy inequalities]], which are central to modern stochastic analysis.<ref name="ResearchGate">{{cite web|title=Burgess Davis's research works|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/Burgess-Davis-2163424493|publisher=ResearchGate|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref>
* [[Brownian motion]] and [[potential theory]]: He explored the relationship between Brownian motion and concepts from [[complex analysis]] and potential theory, including the work on the moments of the lifetime and conditioned Brownian motion in various domains.<ref name="ResearchGate"/>
* [[Random walk]]s: Davis has published research on reinforced random walks, a class of self-interacting random processes where the probability of a step is proportional to the time already spent at the neighboring vertex.<ref name="NYJM">{{cite web|title=NYJM Abstract - 3A-6 - Burgess Davis|url=https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/1998/3A-6.html|journal=New York Journal of Mathematics|date=March 6, 1998|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref>

He has supervised at least seven doctoral students.<ref name="MGP" />

==Awards and honors==
* Davis was named a Top Ten Outstanding Teacher in the College of Science in 1999.<ref name="PurdueStatCV"/>
* He was elected a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], a distinction recognizing individuals who have made "outstanding contributions to the development and application of statistics and probability."<ref name="IMSFellows">{{cite web|title=Honored IMS Fellows|url=https://imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
Davis has published over 50 peer-reviewed articles in major mathematical and statistical journals.<ref name="PurdueStatCV"/> Among them are:
* Davis, B. (1969). Comparison tests for martingale inequalities. ''[[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]'', 40(2), 505–508.<ref name="PurdueStatCV"/>
* Davis, B. (1976). On the <math>L^p</math> norms of stochastic integrals and other martingales. ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]'', 43(4), 697–704.<ref name="PurdueStatCV"/>
* Davis, B. (1979). Brownian motion and analytic functions. ''[[Annals of Probability]]'', 7(6), 913–932.<ref name="PurdueStatCV"/>
* Davis, B., & Volkov, S. (2004). Vertex reinforced random jump processes on trees and finite graphs. ''Probability Theory and Related Fields'', 128(1), 42–62.<ref name="ResearchGate"/>
